full_judgment:
2. The petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 43- 47 of 2014 arise out of the orders dated 20-1-2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division enlarging the respondents on anticipatory bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1329, 1330, 1331, 1332 and 1333 of 2014 respectively. 

 3. In Criminal Petition for leave to Appeal No. 43 of 2014, the respondents obtained impugned order of anticipatory bail in connection with Ramna Police Case No. 7 dated 3-1-2014 under sections 6(2) (A), (Av), (D) 12 of the Santrash Birodhi Ain, 2009. SI Md Ashraful Islam of Ramna Model Police Station lodged First Information Report (in short FIR) against 27/28 unknown persons alleging, inter alia, that at about 6-45 AM on 3-1-2014 some miscreants blasted patrol bombs in a passenger bus bearing registration No. Dhaka Metro-Ja-11-2484 at Paribag area targeting the passengers. Consequently, passengers namely, Md Farid Mia, SahinaAkter and Babul received severe burn injuries. The miscreants also blasted 3/4 patrol bombs to the police personnel. Consequently, SI Md Khaja Mia received, severe burn injuries. The police personnel, with the help of the people, shifted the victims in Dhaka Medical College and Hospital. The respondents instigated and financed the miscreants named in the FIR and others to commit such offence. 

 4. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 44 of 2014, respondents surrendered in the High Court Division in connection with Ramna Model Police Station Case No,42 dated 25-12-2013 under sections 353/333/326/307/302/34/109/114/435/426 of the Penal Code read with section 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 and obtained impugned order of anticipatory bail. One Md Nazmul Islam, SI of Ramna Model Police Station lodged FIR of the said case stating, inter alia, that police constable Md Helal, Ansar Md Quayyum and Ansar Md Nurul Amin were on patrol duty near Banglarnotor area. They were in a bus bearing registration No. Dhaka Metro Ja 06-0215 requisitioned for the use of Police Petrol Party. When that bus reached near traffic box, the miscreants with intention of causing death of police personnel blasted patrol bombs targeting them which caused severe bum injuries to traffic constables Ferdous Khalil and Faijur Islam and Baizid, driver of the bus. They were shifted in Dhaka Medical College and Hospital where the doctor declared Ferdous Khalil dead. The persons including the present respondents named in the body of the FIR planned, conspired and financed the miscreants to commit such offence. 

 5. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 45 of 2014, the respondents surrendered in the High Court Division in Shahbag Police Station Case No. 58 dated 28-11-2013 and obtained impugned order of anticipatory bail from the High Court Division, One Md. Sohel Rahman, SI of Shahbag Police Station lodged FIR with the said police station under sections 326/307/302/ 34/109/114/435/427 of the Penal Code read with section 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 alleging, inter alia, that when a passenger bus of "Bihongo Paribahan" bearing registration No. Dhaka Mctro-Ba-11-3456 was crossing Shishu Park area, the miscreants blasted patrol bombs targeting the passengers of the said bus. Consequently 19 passengers named in the FIR received severe bum injuries. One of the victim namely Md Nahid died at Dhaka Medical College and Hospital. The respondents and other persons, as named in the body of the FIR planned, conspired and financed the miscreants to commit such offence. 

 6. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.46 of 20 14 the respondents surrendered in the High Court Division in connection with Ramna Model Police Station Case No. I dated 1-12-2013 against 15 accused persons named in the FIR and some other unknown miscreants under sections 326/307/302/34/109/114/435/427 of the Penal Code read with section 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 alleging that at about 19-45 hours on 30-11-2003, the FIR named accused’s and others blasted patrol bombs in a bus bearing registration No. Dhaka Metro Ja-11-2639 when the said passenger bus was crossing Malibag Chowdhury para area Consequently, the driver lost the control of the bus. 

 7. The miscreants, with intention of causing death of the passengers of the bus, repeatedly blasted bombs targeting them. The passengers and some other persons, working besides the road, received severe injuries. That offence was committed in compliance with the instigation, plan, conspiracy and finance by the respondents and others as named in the body of the FIR. The High Court Division enlarged the respondents on anticipatory bail by the impugned order. 

 8. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 47 of 2014 the respondent appeared in the High Court Division in connection with Ramna Model Police Station Case No.7 dated 3-1-2014 under section 6(2) (A) (Av) (D)/12 of the Santrash Birodhi Ain, 2009. Facts of this case have been stated earlier. He also obtained anticipatory bail in the High Court Division by the impugned order. 

 10. Mr Shohrowardi submits that the High Court Division while enlarging the respondents on anticipatory bail totally failed to follow the guide lines indicated by this Division in different cases regarding anticipatory bail. The High Court Division also failed to consider the heinousness and brutality of the offences as mentioned in the respective FIR while disposing the applications for anticipatory bail. 

 "Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, allegations made. in the First Information Report as quoted in the application and also submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners and learned Attorney-General, we find prima case in favour of the accused petitioners and, as such, we are inclined to enlarge the accused petitioners on anticipatory bail for a limited period." 

 13. The High Court Division used the quoted sentence in all the Miscellaneous cases while enlarging the respondents on bail. 

 14. This Division in different cases, particularly, in cases of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury reported in 51 DLR (AD) 243 and State vs Zakaria Pintu reported in 31 BLD (AD) 20 = 62 DLR (AD) 420 has given specific indications regarding scope and authority of exercising such extraordinary judicial discretion of the High Court Division. Such discretion has to be exercised with due care and circumspection depending on circumstances justifying its exercise. No blanket order of bail should be passed. Such power of the High Court Division is not unguided or uncontrolled and should be exercised in exceptional cases only. 

 15. Court must apply its own mind to the question and decide whether a case has been made out for granting such relief. Court must not only view the rights of the accused but also the rights of the victims of the crime and the society at large while considering the prayers. An overgenerous infusion of constrains and conditions are not available in the guidelines indicated by this Division in aforementioned cases. 

 16. From the orders of bail of all the cases it appears that the High Court Division has failed to follow the guidelines indicated by this Division while disposing the applications for bail. Orders of anticipatory bail have been passed using words quoted above which cannot be considered as careful and proper exercise of extra-ordinary judicial discretion.
